styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Baths, Parliament, opera and Danube views.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Castle Hill, the Parliament and the Soviet past.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Ruin bars, market halls and hearty Hungarian plates.

stays.why: The flat inner city: walk to the Danube, Váci utca and the Parliament. Best for first-timers.
Quiet cobbled streets on the Buda side, with the palace and Fisherman's Bastion on your doorstep.
Ruin bars, cheap eats and the Great Synagogue; lively and central on the Pest side.
Grand 19th-century streets near the Parliament and Nyugati station; good value and calm at night.

food: Try gulyás (goulash soup), pörkölt stew and lángos flatbread; a filling lunch is often 2500–4500 HUF.
The Great Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok) is good for paprika, sausages and cheap upstairs eats.
Ruin bars in the Jewish Quarter: Szimpla Kert is the famous one; expect busy crowds after dark.
Book a table for dinner on Friday and Saturday; popular places fill up. A mid-range dinner is about 6000–12000 HUF per person.
Budapest is famous for cakes: try a slice of dobos torta or somlói galuska in a traditional café.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for Szentendre: a short suburban train ride up the Danube to a pretty art town.
Bath lovers can add a second thermal bath; the Széchenyi and Gellért baths are the classic picks.
History fans can take a half-day trip to the Memento Park for Soviet statues, or to Esztergom for the basilica.

recommend.why: Three nights covers Castle Hill, the Parliament, a thermal bath and a ruin-bar evening without rushing.

month_notes: January is cold: highs near 4°C, lows around -2°C. Pack a warm coat and gloves.
February stays cold, highs near 8°C. Indoor sights and baths are the plan.
March warms a little to about 12°C. Expect a few rainy days.
April is pleasant at around 17°C; bring a light jacket and an umbrella.
May is lovely, near 21°C, but one of the rainier months.
June is warm at about 26°C; long evenings suit outdoor bars.
July is the hottest month, highs near 28°C. Go sightseeing early and rest midday.
August is as hot as July, around 28°C, with fewer rainy days.
September is warm and dry-ish at about 23°C; a great month to visit.
October cools to around 17°C with some rain; still good for walking.
November turns chilly, near 10°C. Bring layers and a waterproof.
December is cold, highs near 5°C. Christmas markets and baths feel cosy.

climate_guide.summary: Continental climate: cold winters, warm summers, and rain spread through the year.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Warm days from about 21°C to 28°C. Ideal for walking, the river and outdoor bars.

items.title: Cold winters (December to February)
items.text: Highs of 4–8°C and lows near or below freezing. Wear a warm coat, hat and gloves.

items.title: Rain any month
items.text: Expect roughly 8–12 rainy days each month. Carry a small umbrella year-round.

items.title: Summer heat is mild
items.text: July and August peak near 28°C, not extreme. Mornings and evenings are the best times out.

items.title: Spring and autumn are sweet spots
items.text: April–May and September–October give mild temperatures and fewer crowds.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Comfortable walking shoes, layers, a rain jacket, and swimwear for the thermal baths.

transit.best: Metro, trams and walking cover the centre; use the 100E bus for the airport.

modes.text: Lines 1–4 plus trams and trolleybuses cover the centre. Buy tickets or passes at machines and validate every ticket.
Buses and trams are frequent. Bus 100E runs 24 hours between Deák Ferenc tér and the airport. Validate every ticket or risk a fine.
Taxis have fixed citywide rates. Főtaxi is the licensed airport operator, and Bolt works well.
Driving is slow and parking is hard. Skip it for city sightseeing; walking and cycling suit the flat Pest side.
The flat Pest side is easy on foot. Cross the river for Castle Hill, which involves some climbing.
A river ferry and hop-on boats link stops along the Danube.
